source.title: Descending through a Crowded Valley - Benchmarking Deep Learning Optimizers
source.authors: Robin M. Schmidt; Frank Schneider; Philipp Hennig

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation that affects the extracted results.
record.tranche_reason: The benchmark compares optimizers on held-out test performance across deep-learning tasks, providing a different-method test of V4. It does not directly measure the training–test error gap as that version describes.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy or test loss by optimizer, budget, schedule, and task. Those outcomes bear on V4's optimizer comparison. It does not test random-label memorization, width scaling, architecture bias, batch size, dropout, sharpness, or removal of memorized examples. Detailed per-optimizer results are extensive; rows prioritize the two image-classification tasks and the large-budget, no-schedule condition. Table 10 reports training loss, not training accuracy, so it does not directly establish equal or better training performance alongside a test-performance difference.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares held-out performance of adaptive optimizers with SGD and momentum methods. Its broader hyperparameter tuning tests V4's tuning qualification, although it does not reproduce the learning-rate-only tuning condition. A measured training–test gap is not required to test the held-out-performance comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors find no statistically clear universal winner; Adam remains competitive, while NAG and RMSProp improve particular tasks. They also conclude that trying several default optimizers works approximately as well as tuning one optimizer, and that newer methods do not consistently outperform Adam.
record.recipe_differences: The study benchmarks fifteen optimizers over eight DeepOBS problems, four tuning budgets, and four learning-rate schedules. It does not reproduce Wilson et al.'s benchmark design; it uses broad random-search tuning, including schedules and multiple optimizer hyperparameters.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer rankings vary by problem, tuning budget, and learning-rate schedule. The authors report that individual effects vary greatly across optimizers and problems.

fits_no_version.finding: LookAhead(Momentum) outperforms or underperforms plain SGD depending on the task.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Non-adaptive optimization techniques can change held-out performance.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (Proceedings of the 38th International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 139, 2021)
record.problems: The benchmark uses eight DeepOBS tasks and omits ImageNet and transformer models; the authors caution that results may not generalize to other workloads. Hyperparameter search distributions and budgets affect rankings. The study does not directly report paired train–test generalization gaps. Standard deviations are reported for the tabulated test metrics.
record.rows_left_out: The additional task results in Tables 6–9, optimizer/budget/schedule comparisons, and training-loss results in Table 10 were not extracted because of the 60-row cap. Rows retain both CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 large-budget, no-schedule results for all 15 optimizers, except that the provided rows focus on comparisons against SGD and omit Momentum and NAG on CIFAR-10? No: R9–R10 include those. The chosen subset does not include every reported condition or task.

untested.parts: Controlled convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.

The condition tuning only learning rates and decay schedules; optimizer switching; decoupled weight decay; word-level language modeling. Training losses are available, but matched training-error generalization gaps are not reported.
Batch-size interventions and compensating training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removal of memorized examples and retraining.

missing.what: Actual CIFAR-10/3c3d results were mistakenly replaced with Fashion-MNIST results. In Table 6, Adam reaches 82.95 ± 0.70%, SGD 82.64 ± 0.91%, momentum 83.16 ± 0.56%, and NAG 83.30 ± 0.88%. Restore the intended CIFAR-10 rows or explicitly declare their omission.

record.verdict_notes: All supplied values are means ± standard deviations across ten seeds. R1–R14 consistently use the Fashion-MNIST column, not the CIFAR-10 column. Row states describe the comparison with each row's listed SGD baseline; verdicts comparing adaptive methods with momentum additionally use the linked comparator rows. Other tasks, schedules, budgets and Table 10 training results are already declared in rows_left_out, so their omission is not independently flagged as missing. The study is not an original source of V4.

versions.untested_parts: The study compares optimizer test performance, but does not directly analyze the training–test gap or isolate the limited-tuning recipe described in the claim. Some task results are omitted under the 60-row limit.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets.
Sharpness and other measures as predictors of generalization gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: Fashion-MNIST/2c2d, large tuning budget, constant learning rate: adaptive methods that outperform both SGD and momentum
relationships.reason: R1–R5, R8 and R14 reach 92.03–92.26% versus SGD's 91.80% and momentum/NAG's 91.87% (R9–R10), consistent with V4's qualification that broader tuning can reverse the difference.
relationships.display_finding: Adaptive methods achieved mean accuracies of 92.03–92.26% versus SGD's 91.80% and momentum/NAG's 91.87%. The study did not establish whether the accuracy differences between individual methods were statistically significant.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: Fashion-MNIST/2c2d, large tuning budget, constant learning rate: adaptive methods that outperform both SGD and momentum
labels.reason: Table 6 confirms R1–R5, R8 and R14 exceed SGD, Momentum and NAG. This is compatible with V4's broader-tuning qualification, although the comparison does not establish that expanding tuning caused the reversal.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: Fashion-MNIST/2c2d, large tuning budget, constant learning rate: Adam, Nadam, RAdam and RMSProp
labels.reason: R6 and R11–R13 have small numerical deficits under broader tuning, a condition already accommodated by V4. Their standard deviations do not establish statistical equivalence or a new scope limitation.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: CIFAR-100/All-CNN-C, large tuning budget, constant learning rate: adaptive methods versus momentum and NAG
labels.reason: Table 6 confirms R15–R18, R20, R22 and R25–R28 are below Momentum and NAG (R23–R24), showing an adaptive-method test-performance disadvantage even with broader tuning.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: CIFAR-100/All-CNN-C, large tuning budget, constant learning rate: adaptive methods versus plain SGD
labels.reason: Table 6 confirms R15–R18, R20, R22 and R25–R28 exceed plain SGD, consistent with V4's broader-tuning qualification. The result also demonstrates comparator dependence.

labels.label: limits_scope
labels.condition: CIFAR-100/All-CNN-C, large tuning budget, constant learning rate: Adagrad
labels.reason: R19 has worse held-out accuracy than SGD: 43.63 ± 21.35% versus 50.58 ± 1.49%. Table 10 also shows worse, unstable training loss, but V4 does not require comparable training performance for every disadvantage; this does not establish a scope limitation.

relation.reason: Its own test-set results bear on V4, including the broader-tuning qualification; it does not reproduce the original limited-tuning protocol.

tranche.reason: A different benchmark directly compares adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers using held-out performance, with random hyperparameter search, multiple budgets and schedules.

source_check.notes: Value and baseline flags include model/dataset misattribution, even where the numeric transcription is exact. Uncertainties are standard deviations across 10 evaluation seeds; broader tuning is not isolated causally, and pairwise significance is not established.

statements.correction: Table 6: CIFAR-100/All-CNN-C; large tuning budget; constant learning rate; AMSBound 54.64 ± 1.33%, Momentum 56.21 ± 0.67%, NAG 57.85 ± 0.77%, SGD 50.58 ± 1.49%; listed adaptive methods other than Adagrad exceed SGD and trail Momentum/NAG; compatible with V4's broader-tuning qualification; no controlled learning-rate-only versus broader-parameter tuning comparison.
statements.problem: The DeepOBS comparison and its tuning caveat are accurate, but its placement under challenges conflicts with V4's explicit broader-tuning qualification. The ResNet18 and StepLR comparisons concern other studies and are outside this check.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Large-budget, no-schedule image-classification results on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100
reader_labels.reason: Adaptive optimizer test performance varies by task and optimizer: several exceed SGD on CIFAR-100, while Adam, Nadam, RAdam, and RMSProp are at or slightly below the SGD reference on CIFAR-10 (R1–R28). The benchmark does not directly establish training–test gap differences.
